extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, and agency/industry participants preparing or submitting public comments on Federal Register notices (PRA ICRs, NRC SEIS scoping, PRC/USPS dockets)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, obtaining information for, and submitting public comments on Federal Register notices — including PRA information collection requests, NRC SEIS scoping, and Postal Regulatory Commission/USPS filings. Covers what topics to address, how and where to obtain documents, submission methods, privacy cautions, and who may participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA public comment topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are invited on: (1) whether the collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the Department, including whether the information will have practical utility; (2) the accuracy of the agency’s estimates of the burden and cost of the collection of information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used; (3) ways to enhance the quality, utility and clarity of the information collection; and (4) ways to minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who are to respond, including the use of automated collection techniques or other forms of information technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments on the ICR to www.reginfo.gov/public/do/PRAMain (find by selecting “Currently under 30-day Review—Open for Public Comments” or use search). Deadline: OMB will consider written comments received on or before June 23, 2025. Contact: Michael Howell, 202-693-6782 or DOL_PRA_PUBLIC@dol.gov. Citation: Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA).

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Control Number requirement for information collections
rubrics_metrics.description: A Federal agency generally cannot conduct or sponsor a collection of information, and the public is generally not required to respond to an information collection, unless the OMB approves it and displays a currently valid OMB Control Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding other law, no person shall generally be subject to penalty for failing to comply with a collection of information that does not display a valid OMB Control Number. See 5 CFR 1320.5(a) and 1320.6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to obtain documents for NRC action
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicly available information related to this NRC action may be obtained via: the Federal Rulemaking website (https://www.regulations.gov, Docket ID NRC-2025-0076), NRC’s ADAMS (Agencywide Documents Access and Management System), NRC’s Public Document Room (PDR), or at a specified public library location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ADAMS search: select 'Begin Web-based ADAMS Search' or contact PDR reference staff at 1-800-397-4209 / 301-415-4737 or PDR.Resource@nrc.gov. The RNP application and ER accession numbers are provided (e.g., ML25091A290, ML25091A296). Public library: Hartsville Memorial Library address given.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit comments (NRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC encourages electronic comment submission through the Federal rulemaking website (https://www.regulations.gov) and requests that comments include the relevant Docket ID (NRC-2025-0076).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other submission methods: email to RobinsonEnvironmental@nrc.gov; mail to Office of Administration, ATTN: Program Management, Announcements and Editing Staff. For questions about Docket IDs in Regulations.gov contact Bridget Curran (301-415-1003; Bridget.Curran@nrc.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy caution for comment submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC cautions you not to include identifying or contact information that you do not want to be publicly disclosed in your comment submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NRC will post all comment submissions at https://www.regulations.gov and enter submissions into ADAMS and does not routinely edit to remove identifying or contact information. If aggregating or submitting comments for others, inform those persons not to include identifying/contact information they do not want publicly disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC scoping process goals (define proposed action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoping will: define the proposed action that is to be the subject of the SEIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the scoping process as defined in 10 CFR 51.29 and 10 CFR 51.116; public participation is encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC scoping process goals (determine scope and significant issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoping will determine the scope of the SEIS and identify the significant issues to be analyzed in depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scoping comments to raise issues you believe are significant and should be analyzed in the SEIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC scoping process goals (eliminate peripheral issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoping will identify and eliminate from detailed study those issues that are peripheral or are not significant or that have been covered by prior environmental review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should help identify whether an issue is peripheral, insignificant, or already addressed by prior review.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC scoping process goals (identify related EAs/EISs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoping will identify any environmental assessments and other environmental impact statements that are being or will be prepared that are related to, but are not part of, the scope of the SEIS under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide references or identify other relevant environmental reviews in your scoping comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC scoping process goals (identify other review/consultation requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoping will identify other environmental review and consultation requirements related to the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform the NRC of known statutory consultations (e.g., endangered species, cultural resources) that may be relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC scoping process goals (timing and relationship to decision schedule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoping will indicate the relationship between the timing of the preparation of the environmental analyses and the NRC’s tentative planning and decision-making schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments can address schedule-related concerns or timing for analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC scoping process goals (identify cooperating agencies and allocations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoping will identify any cooperating agencies and, as appropriate, allocate assignments for preparation and schedules for completing the SEIS to the NRC and any cooperating agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal/state/Tribal agencies with jurisdiction or special expertise should indicate willingness to be cooperating agencies and what assignments or expertise they can provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC scoping process goals (describe SEIS preparation methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoping will describe how the SEIS will be prepared, including any contractor assistance to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may address adequacy of proposed methods or request disclosure of contractor roles and qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who NRC invites to participate in scoping
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC invites: (a) the applicant; (b) any Federal agency that has jurisdiction by law or special expertise; (c) affected State and local government agencies; (d) any affected Indian Tribe; (e) any person who requests or has requested an opportunity to participate in the scoping process; and (f) any person who has petitioned or intends to petition for leave to intervene under 10 CFR 2.309.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation is encouraged from members of the public and all levels of government; note that participation in scoping does not entitle participants to become parties to the related proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIS evaluation scope and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEIS will evaluate the environmental impacts of subsequent license renewal for RNP and reasonable alternatives thereto; possible alternatives include the no-action alternative and reasonable alternative energy sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEIS will be a plant-specific supplement to NUREG-1437 (Generic Environmental Impact Statement for License Renewal of Nuclear Plants). The ER submitted by the applicant (accession numbers provided) will be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments received after the published deadline will be considered if practical, but the agency can only ensure consideration of comments received on or before the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRC example: submit by June 23, 2025 to ensure consideration. Postal Regulatory Commission example: comments due May 27, 2025 for listed dockets. Always include docket or filing identifiers when submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRC comment scope: statutory/regulatory consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission invites comments on whether the Postal Service’s request(s) are consistent with the policies of title 39 and applicable statutory and regulatory requirements, including 39 U.S.C. 3632, 39 U.S.C. 3633, 39 U.S.C. 3642, 39 CFR part 3035, and 39 CFR part 3041.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should address consistency with the cited statutes/regulations and may reference financial/market impacts under those authorities. Comment deadlines for individual dockets appear in Section II of the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRC submission method and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments electronically via the Commission’s Filing Online system at https://www.prc.gov. Those who cannot submit electronically should contact the person identified in the FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT section for filing alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For more information or to access public portions of filings, use the Commission’s website. Non-public portions require compliance with 39 CFR 3011.301.

rubrics_metrics.name: When public comment is not requested (summary proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to add or amend standardized distinct products are reviewed in summary proceedings pursuant to 39 CFR 3041.325(c)(2) and 39 CFR 3041.505(f)(1); pursuant to 39 CFR 3041.405(c)-(d), the Commission does not appoint a Public Representative or request public comment in such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand whether a filing is subject to a public proceeding (comments invited and Public Representative appointed) or a summary proceeding (no public comment requested). The notice’s Section II vs III distinguishes these.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission appointment of a Public Representative in public proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: For each public proceeding identified, the Commission appoints an officer to represent the interests of the general public (Public Representative) pursuant to 39 U.S.C. 505 and 39 CFR 3000.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Public Representative represents the general public, does not represent any individual or particular viewpoint, and no attorney-client relationship is established when Commission attorneys are appointed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include docket/filer identifiers in comments
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting comments, include the relevant Docket ID or filing identifiers so the agency can associate the comment with the correct proceeding (e.g., Docket ID NRC-2025-0076; PRC docket numbers listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations.gov and other agency submission systems require or strongly prefer docket identifiers; contact information for docket help is provided in the notice.
